q: Your BAC is over .08, or you refuse a breath test. How long is the immediate licence suspension?
a: 90 days
e: Administrative driver's licence suspension (ADLS): 90 days on the spot.
s: Your licence will be suspended immediately for 90 days

q: What blood alcohol range is called the "warn range"?
e: Warn range = .05 to .08. Over .08 is a criminal offence.
s: Drivers who register a blood-alcohol concentration in the “warn range” of .05 to .08

q: A driver with a BAC over .08 has their vehicle impounded for how long?
a: 7 days
e: 7-day impoundment for BAC over .08, or for failing or refusing a police demand.
s: All drivers caught with a BAC over .08, or who fail/refuse to comply with a demand made by a police officer under the Criminal Code of Canada

q: A novice driver breaks a G1/G2 condition for the first time. How long is the suspension?
a: 30 days
e: Escalating sanctions: 30 days, then 90 days, then cancellation.
s: If you violate any of the graduated-licensing conditions, your licence will be suspended for 30 days.

q: Under escalating sanctions, how long is a novice driver's SECOND suspension?
a: 90 days
e: 1st = 30 days, 2nd = 90 days, 3rd = licence cancelled.
s: For a second offence: your driver’s licence is suspended for 90 days.

q: How long is the licence suspension the first time you're convicted of a driving-related Criminal Code offence?
a: 1 year
e: 1 year the first time. Later convictions go up to a lifetime ban.
s: You will receive a one-year licence suspension the first time you are convicted of a Criminal Code offence.

q: If you fail to stop for a police officer, your licence will be suspended for at least…
a: 5 years
e: Failing to stop for police = mandatory suspension, minimum 5 years.
s: If you fail to stop for a police officer (a minimum of five years)

q: You're caught driving while suspended for a Criminal Code offence. The car is impounded for at least…
a: 45 days
e: Minimum 45 days, even if the car was borrowed or rented.
s: If you are caught driving while your licence is suspended for a Criminal Code offence, the vehicle you are driving will be impounded for a minimum of 45 days.

q: Which of these drivers MUST have a blood alcohol level of zero?
a: A 21-year-old with a full G licence
w: A 25-year-old with a full G licence
A 40-year-old with a full G licence
e: All drivers 21 AND under must be at zero, whatever their licence. (A G1's accompanying driver must be under .05.)
s: All drivers who are 21 and under, regardless of licence class, must have a BAC level of zero when operating a motor vehicle.

q: Can you be charged with impaired driving if your car isn't moving?
a: Yes: you can be charged if you're impaired behind the wheel, even if you haven't started to drive
w: No, the car must be moving
Only if the engine is running
Only if you're on a highway
e: Your vehicle doesn't have to be moving.
s: Your vehicle does not have to be moving; you can be charged if you are impaired behind the wheel, even if you have not started to drive.

q: Which of these is NOT a reason for an immediate 90-day licence suspension?
a: Driving 20 km/h over the speed limit
w: Refusing to give a breath sample
e: The 90-day suspension is for alcohol and drug tests: over .08, or failing or refusing a test.
s: If you fail or refuse to perform physical co-ordination tests or submit to a drug evaluation when required by police

q: Your friend lends you their car. You're caught driving it while your licence is suspended (HTA). What happens to the car?
a: It's impounded, even though it isn't yours, and the owner pays the towing and storage
w: Your friend gets a warning letter only
The car is impounded only if it's uninsured
e: Impoundment applies whether the car is borrowed, rented or a business vehicle.
s: These vehicle impoundments apply regardless of whether the vehicle is borrowed from a friend or family member, business, employer or is rented.

q: Is it legal to use a hand-held phone while you're stopped at a red light?
a: No: the law applies while you're stopped in traffic or at a red light
w: Yes, if the light is long
e: Hand-held use is illegal even when stopped. Calling 911 in an emergency is the exception.
s: While you are driving, including when you are stopped in traffic or at a red light, it is illegal to

q: Under Ontario's distracted driving law, which of these IS allowed?
a: Using a hands-free device, like Bluetooth
w: Holding your phone to dial while stopped at a red light
Watching a video on a screen that isn't related to driving
Typing an address into a hand-held GPS
e: Hands-free (earpiece, lapel button, Bluetooth) is allowed. Hand-held use is not.
s: You are allowed to use hands-free wireless communications devices with an earpiece, lapel button or Bluetooth.

q: You're a G2 driver and you've had one beer with dinner. What should you do?
a: Don't drive: use a designated driver, transit, a taxi, or call someone for a ride
e: G2 drivers must have zero alcohol. Plan another way home.
s: have a designated driver

q: Your doctor prescribes a new medicine. What should you do before driving?
a: Ask your doctor or pharmacist about side effects like drowsiness or blurred vision
w: Drive as usual; prescriptions are always safe
e: Some prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
s: Do not take a chance; ask your doctor or pharmacist.

q: When may you drive while your licence is suspended?
a: Never, under any circumstances
w: With a fully licensed driver beside you
e: Driving while suspended brings big fines, possible jail, and 6 more months of suspension.
s: You may not drive, under any circumstances, when your licence is suspended.

q: Who must take the Back on Track program?
a: Drivers convicted of impaired, driving-related Criminal Code offences
e: Back on Track is the required remedial program for impaired driving convictions.
s: The mandatory Back on Track program is for all drivers convicted of impaired, driving-related Criminal Code offences.

q: What happens if you fail or refuse a police demand for a breath, blood, oral fluid or urine sample?
a: You'll be charged under the Criminal Code
w: You must take a driving course
Nothing, unless you were in a crash
e: Refusing is a criminal charge, plus an immediate 90-day suspension.
s: If you fail or refuse to comply with any of these demands, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

q: Which of these will get your licence CANCELLED?
a: Your cheque for licence fees bounces
w: You move to a new address
e: Also: failing a re-exam, not paying a reinstatement fee or penalty, or surrendering your licence.
s: If your cheque for licence fees are not honoured by your bank

q: Ontario's zero-tolerance law for young, novice and commercial drivers also applies to…
a: Cannabis
e: Young and novice drivers must have no alcohol and no drugs in their system.
s: Ontario’s zero-tolerance laws for young, novice and commercial drivers also apply to cannabis.

q: What can a careless driving conviction bring?
a: 6 demerit points, a fine up to $2,000, up to 6 months in jail, and a suspension up to 2 years
e: Careless driving is serious: 6 points.
s: If convicted of careless driving, you may receive

q: Police catch you stunt driving. What happens right away, at the roadside?
a: A 30-day licence suspension and a 14-day vehicle impoundment
e: On conviction it gets worse: a $2,000–$10,000 fine, 6 points and a suspension of 1–3 years.
s: an immediate 30-day driver’s licence suspension

q: A G2 driver is convicted of distracted driving for the first time. What happens?
a: Same fine as other drivers, no demerit points, and a 30-day suspension
e: Novice drivers: 30 days, then 90 days, then cancellation.
s: a 30-day licence suspension for a first conviction
